chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the testimony of a child and a slave, so he said: 'Their testimony is accepted in minor matters on the day they are called to testify, but not in major matters.'

'Ubayd said: And I asked him about the one who is called to testify regarding something when he was a child, having seen it in his childhood, then he stood by it after he grew up. He said: 'His testimony is made better than the testimony of these [adults].'
ai.seo_question: What is the validity of a child's testimony in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between minor (*al-amr al-dun*) and major (*al-amr al-kathir*) legal matters regarding the admissibility of children and slaves as witnesses. It further establishes a hierarchy of testimony, elevating the witness who observed the event in childhood and testified upon maturity above those who witnessed it as adults, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the reliability of long-term memory and consistent presence.
